channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Belgium says evidence points to Iran in its November supermarket fridge attacks, weeks after France blamed the IRGC
item.description: On 12 November Belgium’s interior minister, Bernard Quintin, told parliament that evidence gathered by Belgian authorities points to Iran behind the 2 November attacks that knocked out refrigeration at dozens of Belgian supermarkets, while stressing this is not an official attribution; the foreign minister called one premature. Belgium is the first government to link the November wave, which reached about a dozen European countries, to Tehran. France had already attributed the 11–12 October sabotage of about 700 stores, which caused at least 15 fires and disrupted small hydroelectric sites, to Shahid Kaveh, a unit of Iran’s Revolutionary Guard, and the EU is coordinating a response. Iran rejected France’s accusation. If both waves share a state sponsor, treat every internet-reachable controller, in any sector, as a target. - Arab News, from AFP (12 Nov 2026, Belgian interior and foreign ministers); Cybersecurity Dive via Facilities Dive (11 Nov 2026, EU response); Security Magazine (10 Nov 2026, citing the Wall Street Journal); The Record (9 Nov 2026, French report); SecurityWeek (10 Nov 2026); Anadolu Agency (10 Nov 2026, Iranian denial); Tech Times, citing Reuters (10 Nov 2026, ANSSI findings); CERT-FR - Belgian statement 12 Nov 2026; Belgian attacks 2 Nov 2026; French attribution 9 Nov 2026; October attack 11–12 Oct 2026; Belgian federal investigation and EU response ongoing

item.title: [Critical] CISA and FBI warn of an ongoing threat to internet-connected refrigeration as European supermarket attacks reach at least 11 countries
item.category: Incident — CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT joint warning (5 Nov 2026) and a second wave of refrigeration attacks across about 11 European countries (1–4 Nov); Belgium says its evidence points to Iran (12 Nov), no formal attribution
item.description: Hackers are tampering with internet-connected refrigeration controllers in European supermarkets, and on 5 November CISA and the FBI, with HHS, USDA and DOT, warned the threat is ongoing and also reaches healthcare, chemical, transport and cold-storage operations. Hundreds of French stores were hit in October; a second wave on 1–2 November reached about 11 countries, forcing units into continuous heating or defrost, and three French blood-service sites had settings changed with no blood lost. On 10 November Sweden warned that more incidents are likely after refrigeration was tampered with at seven Coop stores and an undisclosed number of ICA stores on 2 November; its NCSC says the victims mainly ran older systems from one manufacturer protected by weak passwords. On 12 November Belgium’s interior minister said evidence on the Belgian attacks points to Iran but stopped short of an official attribution (see top story); a pro-Russian claim is unverified, and France has formally attributed only the separate 12 October attack, to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard. Exposure is falling but not gone: exposed Danfoss StoreView instances dropped from 3,004 to 708 between 9 October and 5 November (The Hacker News, 9 November). If a controller is reachable from the internet, treat it as at risk today. - TechCrunch (5 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI joint statement); SentinelOne Labs (3 Nov 2026, updated 4 Nov); Cybersecurity Dive (3 Nov 2026, updated with 4 Nov developments); Unit 42 (6 Nov 2026, exposure counts); Censys (6 Nov 2026, exposure analysis); BleepingComputer (5 Nov 2026); Nextgov (29 Oct 2026); Al Jazeera (4 Nov 2026); CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012; The Cyber Express (6 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT advisory summary); Industrial Cyber (6 Nov 2026); Help Net Security (6 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (6 Nov 2026, hardening guidance); The Hacker News (9 Nov 2026, exposure trend); eBuilder Security (11 Nov 2026, Swedish government and NCSC warning); Arab News/AFP (12 Nov 2026, Belgian statement) - Attacks overnight 1–2 Nov 2026; Germany, Romania and UK confirmed 4 Nov 2026; CISA/FBI joint warning 5 Nov 2026; French attribution of the October attack 9 Nov 2026; Swedish government warning 10 Nov 2026; Belgian minister points to Iran 12 Nov 2026 — investigations ongoing

item.title: [Critical] PHP2Shell attacks rooted about two dozen Palo Alto firewalls, and Siemens, Schneider and ABB now list grid-control, DCS and RTU products, several with no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — PHP2Shell chained with a Linux kernel flaw to root exposed PAN-OS firewalls, 23–24 Oct; OT vendor advisories 28–30 Oct
item.description: Palo Alto’s Unit 42 verified on 29 October that a suspected China-nexus actor chained the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) with Linux kernel bug CVE-2026-46300 to gain root on about two dozen internet-exposed PAN-OS firewalls on 23–24 October, then stole Active Directory credentials. Victims were in the US, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea. The OT exposure widened: Siemens now lists Spectrum Power grid-control systems and AMIS TS, Schneider lists a Foxboro DCS server, and ABB lists Netcontrol RTUs and ASPECT gateways, several with no fix yet. Attribution is suspected, not confirmed, and no Siemens, Schneider or ABB product is reported exploited. No OT operator has been named, so treat this as an IT-to-OT boundary warning. - Unit 42 (updated 29 Oct 2026); Palo Alto Networks advisory for CVE-2026-109618 (updated 29 Oct 2026); The Record (29 Oct 2026) and Infosecurity Magazine (30 Oct 2026), citing Dream; CISA KEV catalog (30 Oct 2026 release); Siemens SSA-166980 V1.2 (29 Oct 2026), SSA-566512 V1.1 (28 Oct 2026), SSA-019113 and SSA-082556; Schneider Electric SESB-2026-295-01 v3.2.0 (30 Oct 2026); ABB Netcontrol and Arctic advisories (30 Oct 2026), ASPECT advisory (29 Oct 2026) and APROL SA26P015 (23 Oct 2026); CERT@VDE VDE-2026-127 and VDE-2026-137 - Root compromises 23–24 Oct 2026, verified by Unit 42 29 Oct 2026; KEV additions 26 and 28 Oct 2026; Siemens, Schneider and ABB updates 28–30 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] The Pentagon is treating August freezer failures at US military base stores as a suspected cyberattack, Reuters reports
item.category: Incident — Suspected cyberattack on refrigeration at US military commissaries in late August; reported 29 Oct; cause not confirmed
item.description: Reuters reported on 29 October, citing four unnamed officials, that investigators are treating late-August refrigeration failures at no fewer than six US military commissaries, including Fort Huachuca and Fort Irwin, as a suspected cyberattack: refrigerators and freezers switched to defrost mode and warmed, spoiling food. Army and Air Force investigators, including an Army cybercrime unit, opened inquiries soon after, US Cyber Command has since joined, and one official said investigators have spoken with French police about the October supermarket attack. The Pentagon says it is working closely with interagency and law-enforcement partners and has not confirmed a cause. Reuters could not establish whether the stores used Danfoss equipment, though records for the commissary at Naval Air Facility El Centro list a Danfoss control system. Nextgov/FCW, citing two unnamed sources, reports officials suspect Iran-linked hackers; no agency has attributed it. The entry route and any responsible party are not established. - Reuters (29 Oct 2026), via The Next Web and The Business Standard; Nextgov/FCW (29 Oct 2026) - Published 29 Oct 2026; incidents occurred in late August 2026 — investigation ongoing, cause unconfirmed

item.title: [Medium] Maersk confirms hackers stole data from a legacy system it inherited through an acquisition, as the WhiteArmor gang demands $5 million
item.category: Incident — Data theft from a legacy IT system inherited through an acquisition, confirmed by Maersk 11 Nov 2026; WhiteArmor extortion claim (leak-site listing 7 Nov)
item.description: On 11 November Maersk confirmed that attackers extracted data from a single IT system it inherited through an earlier acquisition, which it did not name. The company says the incident is isolated to that local system, with no sign that other Maersk systems or the customer and partner connections it runs over APIs and EDI were affected, and its booking and shipment platforms remain available. The WhiteArmor ransomware group listed Maersk on its leak site on 7 November, demands $5 million within 30 days, and claims about 100 GB from a platform tied to LF Logistics, the Hong Kong firm Maersk bought in 2022, including driver records with plaintext passwords and staff accounts with administrator rights. Maersk has not confirmed the group, the entry route or the data types, and no terminal, vessel or other OT impact is reported. Acquired companies’ systems that were never fully brought under central security monitoring are a recurring blind spot at logistics and port operators (editorial assessment). - SecurityWeek (12 Nov 2026, Maersk statement of 11 Nov); BleepingComputer (Nov 2026); Smart Maritime Network (12 Nov 2026) - Leak-site listing 7 Nov 2026; Maersk confirmation 11 Nov 2026; reported 12 Nov 2026

item.title: [Info] SANS survey: a third of industrial organizations reported a cyber incident this year, and most of those incidents disrupted operations
item.category: Research — SANS 2026 State of ICS/OT Security survey (released 10 Nov 2026), nearly 700 respondents; no CVE
item.description: The SANS Institute’s 2026 State of ICS/OT Security survey, released on 10 November, found that 34% of nearly 700 industrial respondents had a cyber incident, up from 22% last year and the largest one-year jump in the survey’s history; 72% of those incidents disrupted operations. Shared IT/OT credentials and ransomware tied as the most common incident types (31% each), and incidents affecting safety rose from 8% to 13%. Resilience is thin: only 15% could run critical operations manually for more than 48 hours, 40% do not know, and 58% say they would be unable to operate within a year if their main automation vendor disappeared. A follow-up analysis on 12 November points to a confidence gap: every responding security chief expects plants to keep running through a full IT compromise, yet only 14% of leaders report routine technical validation such as ICS-specific threat hunting, and only 41% of incidents were detected within 24 hours. These are self-reported survey results, not incident data. - SANS Institute via GlobeNewswire (10 Nov 2026); Help Net Security (12 Nov 2026, leadership-versus-practitioner findings) - Published 10 Nov 2026; follow-up analysis 12 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Volt Typhoon has used a rotating “Silent Train” relay network since 2023 to break into management platforms, with water, energy and transport among the victims, Lumen reports
item.category: Threat Intel — Lumen Black Lotus Labs report (28 Oct) on Volt Typhoon’s “Silent Train” relay network and zero-day campaigns against management platforms; water, energy, transportation, maritime, rail and aviation among victim sectors; no OT intrusion described
item.description: Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs reported on 28 October that Volt Typhoon has used “Silent Train”, a covert network of rapidly rotating, single-use chains of compromised small-office routers, IoT and enterprise devices, since November 2023 to reach targets and keep access to management and control-plane systems. Lumen ties the group to four confirmed zero-day campaigns and one likely one: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN (CVE-2026-20127, CVSS v3.1 10.0, Cisco), VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-16812), N-able N-central (CVE-2025-8875 and CVE-2025-8876), Versa Director (no CVE given) and, with moderate confidence, Quest KACE (no CVE). These are older flaws, not the VeloCloud flaw CVE-2026-114625 that CISA added to KEV on 23 October. Victims include telecoms, government, defence contractors, IT firms and MSPs, and universities, and Lumen lists water, energy, transportation, maritime, rail, aviation and emergency services among the critical-infrastructure sectors hit; Hawaii, California and Texas recur as focal points (Zero Day). No victim is named and no OT or ICS intrusion is described. Lumen points defenders to CISA’s Volt Typhoon guidance (AA24-038A) and its advisory on China-nexus covert networks (AA26-113A). Management and orchestration platforms often hold trusted paths into plant networks, which makes them the asset to protect here (editorial assessment). - Lumen Black Lotus Labs (28 Oct 2026); CyberScoop (28 Oct 2026); Zero Day (28 Oct 2026); CISA KEV catalog - Report published 28 Oct 2026; activity tracked since November 2023

item.title: [High] Zyxel GS1900 managed switches: a new zero-day slipped past June’s fix, after attackers had already pulled data from about 1,000 of them
item.category: Threat Intel — Binarly research (reported 5 Nov 2026) on a Zyxel GS1900 switch zero-day, CVE-2026-107441; earlier GS1900 flaw CVE-2026-7273 in CISA KEV; activity tied to a Chinese-speaking group
item.description: Binarly says CVE-2026-107441, an out-of-bounds write in the web-request handler of Zyxel’s GS1900 switches, gives root command execution to anyone who can reach the management interface without logging in, and that attackers already had a working exploit when it reported the bug on 29 September. Zyxel scores it 8.8 (Binarly 9.8). The June firmware that fixed the earlier GS1900 flaw, CVE-2026-7273 (in CISA KEV since 21 September), does not stop it; firmware 2.90 Patch 3, released 23 October, covers 10 models. GreyNoise linked theft of configuration data from 996 GS1900 switches around 17 August to the earlier flaw, and 564 of them still used factory passwords. Acronis ties the activity to a Chinese-speaking group it calls Red Heron, reported to deploy a backdoor and rootkit. Small managed switches like these are common in plant-floor and substation cabinets (editorial assessment). - The Hacker News (5 Nov 2026, Binarly, GreyNoise and Acronis findings); The Hacker News weekly recap (9 Nov 2026); Zyxel advisory - Reported 5 Nov 2026; fixed firmware 23 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] OpenSSH “SSHole” lets an over-long password open password-less accounts on musl-based Linux; exploited within hours and now in KEV
item.category: Advisory — OpenSSH “SSHole” authentication bypass CVE-2026-123158 (CVSS 8.1) on musl-based Linux without PAM; exploited within hours; added to CISA KEV (9 Nov 2026)
item.description: OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes CVE-2026-123158 (CVSS 8.1). On Linux builds that use the musl C library with PAM turned off, a password of 257 to 1,024 characters is accepted for accounts that have no usable password, including root on default Alpine setups. Previdian saw the first attempt less than nine hours after disclosure on 6 November and confirmed root on an Alpine honeypot; by 8 November it counted 20 attempts from 13 addresses, and watchTowr says only botnets and crypto miners have used it so far. CISA has added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Glibc-based distributions, Dropbear and systems that check passwords through PAM are not affected. musl-based embedded builds such as Buildroot, OpenWrt and Yocto sit inside many industrial gateways, routers and appliances, but no OT vendor has yet published an advisory, so whether a given product is exposed depends on how it was built (editorial assessment). - The Hacker News (6 Nov 2026, updated 8 Nov); SecurityWeek (9 Nov 2026); Security Affairs (10 Nov 2026, CISA KEV addition) - Disclosed 6 Nov 2026; KEV addition 9 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens finds the exploited Node2Shell bug in SIMATIC SCADA and PCS 7, and more OT vendors confirm PHP2Shell exposure
item.category: Advisory — ICS Patch Tuesday (11 Nov 2026): Siemens (9 advisories, 10 flaws, two on Node2Shell), Schneider Electric SEVD-2026-314-01, Johnson Controls, Hitachi Energy and Phoenix Contact; CERT@VDE (8 advisories incl. Helmholz, Weidmüller, Beckhoff) and Axis CVE-2026-13312 (10 Nov)
item.description: Siemens published nine advisories on 11 November covering ten flaws, two of them describing how the exploited Node2Shell (Brotli) bug reaches its products. High-severity issues touch SIMATIC SCADA and PCS 7, SIMATIC WinCC Graphics Designer, meta-iot2050, ROS#, Simcenter Femap and the Mendix Studio Pro MCP server, and could allow code injection or system compromise. Several products have no fix yet and some versions will not be fixed, so Siemens points customers to mitigations; it has seen Node2Shell exploitation attempts but no attacks aimed at its products. Schneider Electric fixed a medium-severity file-handling flaw in EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody, Johnson Controls fixed EasyIO Neo IO Manager and a C•CURE 9000/victor installer that could expose admin credentials, and Hitachi Energy and Phoenix Contact confirmed PHP2Shell impact. A day earlier CERT@VDE flagged a dozen bugs in Helmholz’s myREX24V2 remote-access server (fix 2.21.0) and Axis rated a Camera Station flaw 9.9 (CVE-2026-13312). - SecurityWeek ICS Patch Tuesday roundup (11 Nov 2026); Siemens ProductCERT; Schneider Electric SEVD-2026-314-01; CERT@VDE VDE-2026-141 (10 Nov 2026); Axis CVE-2026-13312 advisory (10 Nov 2026) - Published 11 Nov 2026 (Siemens, Schneider, Johnson Controls, Hitachi Energy); 10 Nov 2026 (CERT@VDE, Axis)

item.title: [High] Siemens IoT2050 Node-RED flaw is now being exploited to plant botnet code and command backdoors
item.category: Advisory — Siemens SSA-834709: missing authentication in Node-RED on SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced (CVE-2026-58115, CVSS 10.0); exploitation observed by VulnCheck
item.description: VulnCheck reports exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-58115, a maximum-severity missing-authentication flaw in the Node-RED web interface on SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced gateways running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed. Siemens published the advisory (SSA-834709) on 11 August. An unauthenticated remote attacker can create malicious flows and run code with full privileges. Observed attempts, seen on VulnCheck’s honeypots through 30 October, first downloaded a Linux botnet binary, then used a two-stage loader, and some requests instead created an HTTP endpoint that lets the attacker run commands and survives a reboot. The fix is Node-RED 4.3.4.1 or later; Siemens says to uninstall Node-RED or harden it if you cannot update. Honeypot hits show internet scanning, not confirmed compromise of any plant. A follow-up report on 8 November says Siemens widened the advisory on 4 November to further SIMATIC IoT2050 models when the affected Industrial OS and Node-RED versions are installed (Industrial OS V4.3.4-1 or later is the recommended fix); check the advisory for the current product list. - The Hacker News (3 Nov 2026), citing VulnCheck; Siemens ProductCERT SSA-834709 (11 Aug 2026) - Exploitation reported 3 Nov 2026; advisory 11 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] N-central exploits now reach patched servers: attackers planted miners on 21 servers, 19 of them already running Hotfix 2
item.category: Active exploitation — N-able N-central: new 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell chains reported to work against Hotfix 2; miners found on 21 servers (13 Nov 2026); follows the 9 Nov “Able2Shell” dump of 33 flaws
item.description: On 9 November a researcher published “Able2Shell”, 33 flaws in N-able’s N-central remote monitoring and management platform with proof-of-concept code, and N-able shipped N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 the next day. The same researcher, Sean Bales, has since disclosed two new chains, 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell, that he says work against the latest version; one uses a critical Apache Axis flaw, CVE-2026-90436 (CVSS 9.8). On 13 November Huntback reported cryptocurrency miners on 21 N-central servers, 19 of them on Hotfix 2, mostly in the US, South Africa, Canada, the UK, Germany, France and Sweden, and Previdian described the attack path. N-able is restricting features, has turned off the Legacy API and Intune integration on hosted servers, and tells customers to upgrade Agents and Probes to 2026.4 HF1 or later and disable the Legacy API on premises, with more fixes coming. Many integrators manage plant-side Windows hosts through RMM tools, and a miner today can be a hands-on intruder tomorrow (editorial assessment). - The Hacker News (13 Nov 2026, citing Huntback and Previdian); The Hacker News (12 Nov 2026, new chains); Tenable (Able2Shell FAQ, 10 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (10 Nov 2026); N-able statements - Exploitation reported 13 Nov 2026; new chains disclosed 12 Nov 2026; Able2Shell disclosed 9 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Attackers are pushing rogue ScreenConnect clients through hijacked remote-support panels, reaching 288 endpoints at 48 organizations
item.category: Active campaign — rogue ScreenConnect clients pushed through hijacked cloud-hosted panels, detected 11 Nov 2026; ConnectWise advisory; Blackpoint ties the SCKit toolkit to KEV-listed CVE-2026-84869 (12 Nov)
item.description: Huntress reported on 12 November that, from the evening of 11 November, attackers used the Run Command feature in cloud-hosted ConnectWise ScreenConnect panels to install rogue ScreenConnect clients and a toolkit it calls SCKit on at least 288 managed endpoints across 48 organizations. The malware steals technicians’ session cookies, so a technician who connects to an infected machine can hand the attacker access to other customer sessions, letting it spread from client to client. Huntress suspects stolen credentials or hijacked sessions, and ConnectWise says it has found no compromise of its own infrastructure. Separately, Blackpoint Cyber said on 12 November that SCKit exploits CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9), a ScreenConnect flaw patched and added to CISA KEV in September, and that a fully patched client blocks its payload. No industrial victim is named, but many integrators and service providers support plant systems through ScreenConnect, so a compromised technician is a direct path into OT (editorial assessment). - Huntress (12 Nov 2026); Blackpoint Cyber via The Hacker News (12 Nov 2026); ConnectWise advisory; Sophos alert; The Hacker News (12 Nov 2026) - Activity detected 11 Nov 2026; reported 12 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Fortinet details eight critical flaws in FortiGate firewalls and FortiManager, including routing-protocol bugs it fixed quietly in October
item.category: Advisory — Fortinet November PSIRT (10 Nov 2026): eight critical flaws across FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer, fixed in October builds; no exploitation reported, not in CISA KEV
item.description: On 10 November Fortinet published details of eight critical vulnerabilities, most of them fixed in builds it shipped around 21–22 October while asking customers to patch before details were out. The highest, CVE-2026-126170 (CVSS 9.8), is in the JSON RPC API of FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer, which is off by default. In FortiOS, CVE-2026-126254 (9.6) is a numeric truncation bug in the BGP daemon, CVE-2026-126253 (9.3) bypasses OSPF authentication, and CVE-2026-126259 (9.0) is missing authentication in high-availability sync on specific FGSP or autoscale setups. The rest hit FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer through SQL injection and SSRF over OFTP, FGFM authorization and cross-VDOM access. Fortinet reports no exploitation, but researchers expect the fixes to be reverse-engineered quickly now that details are public. FortiGate is a common IT/OT boundary firewall, and FortiManager often manages plant firewalls centrally, so one compromised manager can reach many sites (editorial assessment). - SecurityOnline (10 Nov 2026, summarising Fortinet’s November PSIRT advisories); Fortinet PSIRT; SecurityWeek (11 Nov 2026) - Advisories published 10 Nov 2026; fixes shipped 21–22 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Citrix fixes a dozen NetScaler flaws, including nine critical gateway memory bugs and a Console login bypass
item.category: Advisory — Citrix security bulletins (12 Nov 2026): nine memory-safety flaws in NetScaler ADC and Gateway rated CVSS 9.3–9.5, a NetScaler Console authentication bypass (9.4) and two Secure Access Client privilege escalations; no exploitation reported, not in CISA KEV
item.description: On 12 November Citrix patched 12 vulnerabilities across its NetScaler line. Nine are memory overflow or corruption bugs in NetScaler ADC and Gateway scored CVSS 9.3 to 9.5; one, CVE-2026-120868 in packet processing, affects every deployment, while the others depend on specific setups such as Gateway or AAA virtual servers, Endpoint Analysis, ICA proxy, DNS-over-HTTPS or Email OTP. Citrix describes the impact as denial of service or unpredictable behaviour. Separately, CVE-2026-120869 (9.4) lets an unauthenticated attacker bypass login on NetScaler Console, and two Secure Access Client bugs (8.5) allow local escalation to SYSTEM or root. Citrix says it knows of no exploits. NetScaler Gateway is a common front door for vendor and engineer remote access into plants, and attackers exploited other NetScaler flaws within weeks in August and September, so treat these as boundary-critical (editorial assessment). - The Hacker News (12 Nov 2026, summarising Citrix’s security bulletins); Citrix security bulletins - Bulletins and fixes published 12 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] PTC patches a critical remote-code flaw in Windchill and FlexPLM, months after a similar bug was exploited for data extortion
item.category: Advisory — PTC Windchill and FlexPLM: CVE-2026-126325 (CVSS v4 9.2), remote code execution via deserialization; patched 12 Nov 2026; no exploitation reported, not in CISA KEV
item.description: On 12 November PTC fixed CVE-2026-126325 (CVSS v4 9.2), an input-validation and deserialization flaw that lets crafted requests run code on Windchill and FlexPLM servers, the product-lifecycle systems many manufacturers use to hold designs, bills of materials and engineering change records. Affected releases run from 11.0 M030 through 13.1.4.0 for Windchill and 13.1.3.0 for FlexPLM. PTC has patched its hosted environments and urges self-hosted customers to patch as soon as possible. No exploitation is reported, but an earlier Windchill/FlexPLM flaw, CVE-2026-12569, was exploited by Cl0p-linked actors in a data-extortion campaign, so expect attackers to study this fix. A compromised PLM server exposes the engineering data that plants build to, and often connects to manufacturing systems (editorial assessment). - The Hacker News (12 Nov 2026), citing PTC’s advisory - Patched and disclosed 12 Nov 2026

item.title: [Info] Comments close 30 November on NIST’s draft rewrite of its OT security guide, which adds water, food, rail, maritime and building-automation coverage
item.category: Guidance — NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 4 draft (released 21 Sep 2026); public comments close 30 Nov 2026; no CVE
item.description: NIST’s draft Revision 4 of SP 800-82, the US government’s main guide to operational technology security, is open for public comment until 30 November 2026. The draft reorganises the guide around Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with risk management now led by the Govern function, and adds sector material for building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail, maritime vessels, and industrial IoT connected to cloud services. It also expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and detection, protecting system-management functions, and applying zero-trust principles. Many regulators, insurers and auditors use 800-82 as a reference, so its final wording can shape what operators are asked to show; the comment window is the chance for practitioners to flag guidance that would not work on a plant floor. - NIST CSRC, SP 800-82 Rev. 4 initial public draft (21 Sep 2026); SecurityWeek (24 Sep 2026) - Forward-looking: public comments close 30 Nov 2026

item.title: [Info] UK cyber agency judges an AI-assisted ransomware attack on critical national infrastructure highly likely by 2028, after 80 nationally significant incidents this year
item.category: Policy — UK NCSC Annual Review 2026 (published 11 Nov 2026, covering the year to September 2026); no CVE
item.description: The UK National Cyber Security Centre’s annual review, published on 11 November, says it is highly likely that AI-powered malware will have been used in a ransomware attack on UK critical national infrastructure, such as energy, water and transport, by 2028, and that China, Russia and other states will routinely use AI in cyber operations by then. It expects AI mainly to speed up and scale existing attack methods rather than create new ones. The review recalls the December 2025 attack on Poland’s energy grid, which the UK and EU attributed to Russia’s FSB Centre 16 and which could have cut power to about 500,000 people, and notes that the same unit targets infrastructure networks worldwide through vulnerable routers. In the year to September the NCSC handled 80 nationally significant incidents, about one every five days. - NCSC Annual Review 2026 (11 Nov 2026); PublicTechnology (11 Nov 2026) - Published 11 Nov 2026; covers the 12 months to September 2026

item.title: [Info] CISA launches an Installed Base Program to work with OT manufacturers on finding and securing their internet-exposed equipment
item.category: Program — CISA Installed Base Program (announced 10 Nov 2026); voluntary partnership with OT manufacturers; no CVE
item.description: On 10 November CISA announced the Installed Base Program, a voluntary partnership with original equipment manufacturers to identify internet-exposed OT devices across critical infrastructure and get them secured. The approach pairs what CISA sees on the internet with what manufacturers know about where their products are installed, so that owners can be warned sooner. Where it cannot tell who owns an exposed device, CISA says it may use administrative subpoenas to identify the owner. The launch follows weeks in which exposed refrigeration controllers were sabotaged at scale (see Incidents & Attacks). Operators should expect more direct notices, from CISA or their vendors, about equipment they may not know is reachable. - CISA Installed Base Program page; Industrial Cyber (Nov 2026); Viakoo Daily OT Security News via Security Boulevard (11 Nov 2026) - Announced 10 Nov 2026
